candidates.name: city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration
candidates.what_it_holds: Git-scraping repo (Simon-Willison-style) that pulls the City of Toronto open-data portal's official 'Short Term Rentals Registrations' CSV (short-term-rental-registrations-data.csv) every day at UTC midnight and commits it. Active as of 13 Sep 2026 (last updated 2026-09-13). Because it commits a fresh CSV daily, the git commit history itself is a genuine point-in-time vintage series of Toronto's STR registration list (registration IDs/status/addresses per the city schema) going back to whenever the repo started running. Has a LICENSE file (type not confirmed) and a short README describing the git-scraping method.
candidates.why_useful: Toronto is a named target in gap #12 (city registration datasets: Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal/Quebec CITQ...). This is not just a one-time dump but a running, dated, point-in-time capture of the actual regulator's registry — directly usable to build a Toronto STR active-listing/registration count time series without needing to scrape the city ourselves (satisfies rule 2's point-in-time requirement and rule 6's sanctioned-sources constraint, since the underlying pull is of a government open-data portal, not airbnb.com).
candidates.time_coverage: Daily snapshots from repo creation to current (last commit 2026-09-13); exact start date not confirmed from README excerpt
candidates.size_hint: One CSV per commit; commit history length unconfirmed (would need `git log` on a clone to count — not done here per no-clone rule)
candidates.license: LICENSE file present, exact license text not read

candidates.name: Toronto-Short-Term-Rentals
candidates.what_it_holds: A README + one Jupyter notebook ('Toronto Short Term Rentals.ipynb') doing exploratory analysis of Toronto's short-term rental registration data; description says 'Toronto short term rental registration data exploration'. Last updated 2021-10-04; effectively dormant. No confirmed committed CSV — the notebook likely pulls from the city's open-data portal itself, making this at most a reference/method rather than a stored panel.
candidates.why_useful: Secondary/backup pointer to the same Toronto STR registration open-data source; low incremental value given the RamVasuthevan repo above is actively maintained and git-scraped, but worth noting as a second confirmation that Toronto's registration data is the same dataset multiple people have pulled.
candidates.size_hint: One notebook, no confirmed data file
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying source as city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration above, but stale and one-shot rather than a vintage series

notes: This theme hit a very thin GitHub surface: targeted terms (CITQ, NSW STRA, BC registry, Montreal STR, Melbourne STR) returned zero gh search results across multiple phrasings, and government open-data portals for these registries (Toronto Open Data, NSW STRA public register, Registre du tourisme/CITQ, BC short-term rental registry) do not appear to have GitHub mirrors or client libraries that surface in repo search the way Austin/Barcelona/California TOT ones do. Hit GitHub search API rate limiting twice (403) mid-run; waited ~40s and retried successfully per protocol. WebSearch tool was already at its session-wide budget cap (200/200) when I reached this theme, so I could not fall back to web search for CITQ/NSW-specific terms as instructed — this is a hard blocker, not a dead end I chose. The one strong find (RamVasuthevan's Toronto git-scraping repo) is a genuine point-in-time win worth flagging to whoever runs the WS4/vintage-register work: a live, dated, government-source STR registration series that could seed the point-in-time discipline (rule 2) for at least one Canadian city. Recommend a follow-up scout with WebSearch budget available (or `gh search code` sparingly) specifically for: 'NSW Fair Trading STRA register', 'Quebec CITQ registre tourisme scraper', 'BC short-term rental registry API', and 'Montreal reglement location court terme' plus French-language terms, since Quebec/Montreal sources are likely to be indexed under French keywords that this scout did not have budget to try. Also worth checking Toronto Open Data's own CKAN/Socrata API directly (gap #17 tooling) rather than only GitHub, since it may expose historical snapshots beyond what git-scraping repos capture.
